title: Left finite scalar quotient formula
statement:
theorem left_quotient_formula_exists
    (b : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ leftComplex l E L ι g ≅
      (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ rightComplex l E L ι g)
    (hb : CompletedFormula l E L ι g b) :
    ∃ vleft : ∀ n : ℕ,
        (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ leftComplex l E L ι g ⟶
          (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ restrictedLeft l E L ι g n,
      LeftQuotientFormula l E L ι g vleft

proof.text: Apply finite_formula_unit_exists to obtain the finite comparison with its unit middle-coefficient formula, and right_quotient_formula_exists to obtain the right completed-to-finite map with its pure-tensor formula. Only the unit case of the finite comparison is needed.

The defining completed coefficient limit map commutes with each finite projection. Compose this identity with the inverse completed and finite coefficient isomorphisms, and evaluate on a local coefficient section s, to obtain cB inverse(piX(cS(s))) = piY(s). This is inverseCoefficient_square in the existing inverse-image pullback comparison module.

Let e_n be the finite comparison after restriction to completed L coefficients. Define vleft_n = b.hom followed by vright_n followed by e_n.inv. This is already a natural transformation of cochain functors. On a completed pure tensor use CompletedFormula, then RightQuotientFormula. The unit finite formula evaluated at piX(cS(s)), together with the coefficient identity of the preceding step and map_one, identifies e_n.hom of the desired double pure tensor with this result. Apply e_n.inv and cancel e_n.hom followed by e_n.inv. This proves LeftQuotientFormula without any extra statement or flatness/surjectivity assumption.
